Performers
Susan Kavinski (soprano (Chief Musician)), Richard Reed (English horn (Chief Musician)), United States Navy Concert Band (ensemble) Documented

As stated in the Commons description. No conductor is named in the consulted sources.

[1]
Work version
Arrangement for soprano, English horn solo and concert band; arranger not identified Inferred, not documented

Commons names the Navy Concert Band, a soprano and an English horn but does not name an arranger or edition. Mahler wrote the song for voice with piano or orchestra, so a band performance implies an arrangement. This recording’s chroma estimates read F major, whereas the first-edition orchestral score on IMSLP (22552) is notated in E♭ major; IMSLP lists the song in F major and notes transposed publications. The estimates suggest a possible pitch difference from that edition, but neither the arrangement’s key nor any transposition has been confirmed.

[1] [3]
Recorded
c. December 2020 Documented

Commons gives the performance date as c. December 2020 and says the performance was “for the 2020 Midwest Clinic held in December 2020”. The exact session date of the pre-recorded virtual event is not stated.

[1]
Place
Unknown Unknown

No recording venue is named in the consulted sources.

Transfer
Audio taken from YouTube video Dcua8t6J7bE and uploaded to Wikimedia Commons by the user Mysterymanblue. Documented

From the Commons Source field and file history. The YouTube page itself was not opened for content (the reader returned no metadata or transcript).

[1] [2]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

The date of extracting or encoding the audio from the source video is not documented. 14 March 2021 is the documented Commons upload date (file history), not a known extraction or transfer date.

[1]
Processing
Audio extracted from a YouTube video and encoded as Ogg Vorbis (Xiph.Org libVorbis I 20200704, 390 kbps); streamed as an MP3 derivative generated by Commons. Documented

From the Commons file page and metadata. Audio taken from an online video has already passed through the video platform’s lossy coding; no restoration or noise reduction is documented.

[1]
Composition rights
Public domain: Mahler died in 1911 and the poet Friedrich Rückert in 1866. Documented

Commons applies PD/1923 tags to both the composition (author died 1911) and the lyrics (author died 1866). These cover the song and poem, not the unidentified band arrangement.

[1]
Recording rights
Public domain in the United States as a work of a U.S. Navy sailor or employee made as part of official duties (Commons template PD-USGov-⁠Navy); the file also carries the Public Domain Mark. Documented

This is a status under United States law for works of the federal government, as stated on Commons. The copyright status of the band arrangement itself is not addressed by the Commons tags and the arranger is unidentified.

[1]

United States Navy Concert Band, with Susan Kavinski (soprano) and Richard Reed (English horn); performance c. December 2020, via Wikimedia Commons. Public domain as a work of the U.S. Navy; arranger not identified. Rights statement
